venue.name: Kelp Reef Adventures
venue.description: Kelp Reef Adventures runs guided sea kayak tours from a floating dock at Fisherman's Wharf, Dock A, 1 Dallas Road in Victoria, about fifteen minutes on foot from downtown. Tours paddle the sheltered Inner Harbour or head out of the harbour along the coastline towards the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with chances of seeing harbour seals, river otters, great blue herons and bald eagles. All the gear is provided, including lifejackets, spray skirts, paddling jackets, gloves and drinking water, and every tour starts with a safety briefing and a paddling lesson. The youngest paddler they take is 7 on the two hour and family tours and 12 on the three hour tour, so none of the tours are open to daycare age children.
venue.address: Fisherman's Wharf, Dock A, 1 Dallas Rd. Victoria, BC, Canada

facility_notes.washrooms: The site does not mention washrooms of its own. It says of a neighbour, the Greater Victoria Harbour Authority, that public washrooms are available April to October.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is pay parking available or walk the scenic pedestrian walkway from downtown, just 15 minutes.

venue.nearby_park: Fisherman's Wharf park, adjacent to the wharf
restrictions: Children must be accompanied by an adult on the Family Tour.
venue.seasonal_notes: Tour times change with the season. The 4pm departure runs May to September 15, and the 7pm departure and the 11am three hour tour run June to August 31. The Family Tour runs every day at 4pm from June 1 to August 31.

programs.name: 3 Hour Kayak Tour
programs.description: A three hour guided kayak tour covering six miles, described by the site as an active tour. It leaves the harbour for Victoria's coastline and the nearby islands, and the morning is the calmest time to go because the wind is usually lightest. July through September is pupping season, when there is a chance of seeing female harbour seals with their young. Children 12 years and older. The price is $120.00 per paddler and reservations are required.
programs.what_children_do: Get fitted with a lifejacket and spray skirt on the floating dock, take a safety briefing and a lesson on paddling and steering, then paddle six miles out of the harbour and along the coast, watching for harbour seals hauled out on the rocks.
programs.our_note: Twelve and over only, six miles of paddling and no easy place to stop halfway, so this is for a group that has kayaked before. The 9am departure gets the calmest water, which matters more than it sounds when there are children in the boats.
programs.practical_summary: Everything happens on the water with all the gear provided, so there is no indoor space and no rain plan described. They do not mention washrooms of their own, and the site publishes no group rate, no maximum group size and no notice period, so call before you plan a class outing.
programs.cancellation_note: Please allow 24 hours notice of change or cancellation of your tour. No shows will be charged.
programs.evidence: Children 12 years and older. Reservations required.

programs.name: 2 Hour Kayak Tour
programs.description: A two hour guided kayak tour covering less distance than the three hour tour. Depending on the wind it either heads out into the Strait of Juan de Fuca or explores Victoria's Inner Harbour, with chance encounters with harbour seals, river otters and many types of shore birds. Children 7 years and older. The price is $80 per paddler and reservations are required. The 1pm departure is listed daily, the 4pm departure runs May to September 15 and the 7pm departure runs June to August 31.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a lifejacket and spray skirt on the floating dock, learn how to hold the paddle and steer, then paddle for two hours through the harbour or out past the breakwater, looking for seals, otters and shore birds.
programs.our_note: The youngest they take is 7, so a daycare group is out. Two hours on open water with no way to stop early asks a lot of a child who tires, so this suits an older group that will keep paddling.
programs.practical_summary: It all happens on the water with the gear provided, so there is no indoor space and no rain plan described. They do not mention washrooms of their own, and no group rate, group size limit or notice period is published.
programs.cancellation_note: Please allow 24 hours notice of change or cancellation of your tour. No shows will be charged.
programs.evidence: Children 7 years and older. Reservations required.

programs.name: Family Tour
programs.description: A leisurely 90 minute paddle through the sheltered waterways of Victoria's harbour in stable double kayaks, with two paddlers on board so it is easier for smaller paddlers. It follows a brief lesson and orientation. Children must be accompanied by an adult. Children 7 to 12 years old are $40, which the site describes as half price, and reservations are required. It runs every day at 4pm from June 1 to August 31.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the front of a double kayak with an adult behind them, take a short lesson on the dock, then paddle for about ninety minutes around the sheltered parts of the harbour.
programs.our_note: The $40 is the children's price for ages 7 to 12 and an adult shares the same double kayak, so budget a full price seat for every adult you bring. It only runs at 4pm from June to the end of August, which is late in the day for a childcare group.
programs.practical_summary: It all happens on the water with the gear provided and no indoor space or rain plan described. The adult price for this tour is not published, and they do not mention washrooms of their own, so ask about both when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $40 is the rate for children 7 to 12. The adult rate for this tour is not published.
programs.cancellation_note: Please allow 24 hours notice of change or cancellation of your tour. No shows will be charged.
programs.evidence: Children 7-12 years old are $40. Reservations required.

images.alt: Four paddlers in red and yellow sea kayaks on calm harbour water, with moored sailboats and the domed Legislature building behind them.
Kayaks stacked on wooden racks along a floating dock with a Canadian flag on a post, three people standing on the dock and a guide holding a paddle beside a yellow kayak in the water.

gaps: the site sets a minimum age of 7 on the two hour and family tours and 12 on the three hour tour, which rules out daycare and preschool groups entirely
nothing on the site mentions school groups, group bookings or a group rate, so whether a class can be taken as a block is unknown
no maximum or minimum group size is published for any tour
no minimum notice or lead time for a reservation is published; the site says only that reservations are required
the adult price on the Family Tour is not published; only the $40 rate for children 7 to 12 is given
there is no address postal code and the site publishes no map embed or coordinates, so the location needs geocoding from the street address
the site does not mention washrooms of its own. It says of a neighbouring business, the Greater Victoria Harbour Authority, that public washrooms are available April to October
no indoor space, shelter or rain plan is described, and the site does not say what happens to a booking if the weather turns
the site does not say what happens if a kayak capsizes or what the guide to paddler ratio is
the most recent blog post on the site refers to being open for the 2018 season, so the times and prices on the home page are worth confirming when you book
no photograph on the site carries alt text; the two recorded here were looked at in a browser before their descriptions were written
